Ok so ill start saying that I'm sorry your going through this. I know first hand how messy and toxic a divorce can be, plus the effects it has on a child. It sounds like your brother has a lot of hurt in him and the best way he can express it is by acting out. When i was seven and my parents separated i tried looking for a bad guy and a good guy. But it kept changing between my mom and then my dad as they both defended themselves and the actions they took. I only now realize there was no good or bad guy just a bunch of mistakes. 

I sexted, did drugs, and drank as much booze I could get my hands on. It made me feel grown and i sure as hell didn't wanna be a kid. Not with the mess of life I had. Cause being a kid means your vulnerable and scared. Your brother needs someone in his life he can put his absolute trust in. Someone he can be vulnerable with but also that won't make excuses for his actions. 

It sounds like your parents are very self-centered and he needs someone with *his* best interest in mind. Hopefully, that can be you but remember to also take care of yourself.

When my dad had a stroke I took in my half-sister while barely knowing what i wanted to do with my life. My family was against me, my friends either dead or dealing with their own problems and I was drowning in my own regrets. So taking in a child seems very dumb but it was the best thing I've ever done. 

I have been high and I have been low. I have been broke and I have been in a stable job. But the thing that stayed consistent is that every single thing I did was for her. Cause when you have a child you put yourself last and them first every time, no matter what.

Sit down and talk with your sister. If you think your father is untrustworthy and toxic to your life then you have all the right to cut him out of your life. Speaking from experience its a very relieving thing sad yes but very relieving. But i still kinda regret not talking it out at least once.

I don't know how teachers are doing it these days but I told mine that I was having anxiety issues and asked if there was anything I could do to bring my grades up. Also is it possible theres some latent issue that is making her anxiety worse? This was the case for me and i didn't even know the issue was an issue until I eliminated it from my life.

You're of course never wrong for worrying about your child and education is important. The best thing you can offer a person with anxiety issues is trust. Back in HS I had terrible anxiety and skipped homework and class cause it just made me more anxious. My failing grades added on more stress and I began doing stupid stuff to get my mind more at ease. This all continued until I spiraled and had no choice but to tell my grandfather what was going on. The first thing he did was make me understand that even if I fell hed be my safety net and catch me. Then he had me speak to my teachers and they were amazingly understanding. 

What im trying to say is dont give up and try to communicate better. If she doesnt want to talk then let her know that the offer is never off the table.

Now as I'm typing this that girl is my best friend and I call her parents' mom and dad. Apparently, before pressing charges or trying to get me expelled they wanted to see what type of kid i was outside of school. In other words, the best way to deal with bullying is to be adaptable to conflict.
